thread:
alex_support: Hey team — incoming from a customer in EU region: they see perfectly valid streaming JSON from our hosted API but the client ends up with a truncated JSON blob (missing final brace and no finish_reason). They can repro consistently when going through their Cloudflare worker proxy. Full details below.

anna_support: Customer report summary: chat streaming, last chunk missing ~30-40 bytes, client-side JSON parse fails. Customer sent logs and a small repro. Says it happens ~1 in 8 streams.

alex_support: Key snippets from their client logs:
```
SSE chunk received (partial): \"{\"id\":\"abc123\",\"choices\":[{\"delta\":{\"content\":\"This is the last sentence that gets cut off\"
client: JSON parse error: Unexpected end of input
```
They also captured raw HTTP/2 frames via `nghttp` showing `RST_STREAM (REFUSED_STREAM)` right after the last data frame.

sara_engineer: Possible causes: upstream connection reset or proxy idle timeout dropping stream before we've sent final `\n\n` terminator. Could also be token refresh/401 mid-stream causing server to close stream. Does customer show any 401 in logs?

tim_client: They said no 401s. Their Cloudflare worker logs show `H2 RST_STREAM` when response body length is ~512KB; otherwise fine. Not seeing app-level errors.

mike_infra: I'm seeing similar on our infra metrics: brief spike of `stream_reset` events for that POP around these times. infra-monitor-bot: alert: pop-eu-2 h2_rst_rate: 12/min (1m avg).

sara_engineer: Repro plan from engineering: 1) curl with `--http2` via Cloudflare worker, 2) capture raw bytes at client, 3) repeat without proxy to compare. We should reproduce locally with a small worker script to simulate their path.

alex_support: Customer provided a minimal worker snippet they're using:
```
addEventListener('fetch', event => {
  return event.respondWith(handle(event.request))
})

async function handle(req) {
  const upstream = await fetch('https://api.redwood.example/v1/stream', {headers: req.headers})
  const r = new Response(upstream.body, {status: upstream.status, headers: upstream.headers})
  return r
}
```
They don't mutate body, so it's a passthrough.

mike_infra: Two hypotheses: 1) Cloudflare worker has a hard limit/timeout on long-lived h2 streams and sends RST_STREAM, 2) our server doesn't flush a final chunk in some code paths so the proxy considers stream idle and kills it.

sara_engineer: I instrumented our runtime on a dev branch to force a `flush()` after the final SSE event and added an explicit `\n\n` termination. Patch: ensure we send a final empty `data:\n\n` event and call `res.flush()` on the underlying socket. Pushed a test build to staging.

deploy-bot: deploy queued: staging/stream-finish-flush -> running canary (3/3).

sara_engineer: Staging canary results: with the patch plus keepalive pings the issue disappears under Cloudflare worker simulation. Without patch, still saw ~1/12 streams get truncated.

anna_support: Customer asked about workarounds while we investigate. Suggested options: 1) disable worker proxy, 2) enable Cloudflare `stream`/`disable_connection_reuse` setting, 3) implement client-side retry that buffers partial and retries using `Range`/resume? They prefer not to disable proxy.

tim_client: They tried enabling `keepalive: true` on their fetch in the worker and saw improvement but still rare failures.

mike_infra: Also found this in proxy logs — our backend sent `Content-Length: chunked` SSE and final chunk length reported 0 but we didn't flush due to edge-case when generated final message empty (finish_reason suppressed). So proxy may consider stream complete and close slightly early.

sara_engineer: Action items:
- ship flush/terminator patch to prod (sara, mike)
- add a short keepalive ping every 15s for long streams (mike)
- add telemetry counter for streams closed with `rst_stream` and `no_finish_flag` to help correlate (sara)
- share mitigation with customer (anna)

alex_support: Proposed customer communication: explain root cause likely proxy-induced stream reset; we have a server-side fix to ensure final SSE terminator + force flush; asking if they can test with the next build in ~1 hour or try enabling keepalive. Also offer to whitelist their worker POP to test.

anna_support: I'll send a note with repro steps and a temporary mitigation guide (enable keepalive + client retry).

tim_client: Customer follow-up: willing to test patch. They asked whether this might be related to billing/auth — they saw a token refresh happen for other unrelated requests at the same time but not for the stream. I confirmed auth not used mid-stream.

sara_engineer: Post-mortem note for later: streaming protocols over intermediaries (Cloudflare, Envoy) can translate HTTP/2 resets differently. Always send explicit stream terminators and periodic pings; treat `REFUSED_STREAM` as transient and support client-side resume or idempotent retry tokens.

mike_infra: Deploying to prod in 30. I'll update here once done.

alex_support: Thanks all — please copy me on the customer message.

deploy-bot: deploy complete: prod/stream-finish-flush v1.2.4 -> success.

mike_infra: Patch live. Early telemetry: rst_stream rate in pop-eu-2 down from 12/min to 0.4/min.

anna_support: Customer confirmed after testing: saw zero truncations in 200 streams. Closing for now but asked we keep an eye on the metric and follow up if anything else pops up. :thumbsup:
